title: International Gita Mahotsav 2026 runs at Kurukshetra from 5 to 25 December
dek: Haryana's three-week festival around the Bhagavad Gita will have West Bengal as a partner state and, for the first time according to officials, cultural programmes at Jyotisar as well as Brahma Sarovar.
body: The International Gita Mahotsav will be held in Kurukshetra, Haryana, from 5 to 25 December 2026, UNI reported on 29 October and 9 November, quoting state officials. The main programme is set for 14 to 20 December, and UNI gives 20 December as the day Gita Jayanti is observed this year.

The festival is organised by the Government of Haryana with the Kurukshetra Development Board. According to the festival's official website, the board began a Gita Jayanti celebration in the town in 1989, and it has carried the name International Gita Mahotsav since 2016.

Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini announced this year's plans at the 83rd meeting of the board's governing body chaired by Governor Asim Kumar Ghosh, UNI reported on 29 October. UNI named West Bengal and Delhi as partner states and said a public outreach campaign would cover 182 sacred sites in the 48-kos Kurukshetra region. A PTI report of 18 November, carried by DD India, names West Bengal as the partner state and does not mention Delhi.

According to PTI, the main cultural programmes have so far been held at Purushottampura Bagh beside Brahma Sarovar; this year, for the first time, officials said, cultural programmes will also be staged at Jyotisar, the tirtha that tradition identifies as the place where the Gita was taught. PTI lists a Haryana pavilion, the Saras and Shilp melas, seminars on the Gita, a depiction of Krishna's Virat Swaroop, and a light and sound show, and quotes Deputy Commissioner Vishram Kumar Meena as saying that 18 gates, one for each chapter of the Gita, will be built at the venue.

The full schedule and the names of performers and seminar speakers had not been published in the reports we read. The festival's website links to an IGM 2026 schedule page, which readers can check closer to the dates.
place: Brahma Sarovar and Jyotisar, Kurukshetra, Haryana
